title: Colombia Formally Closes Total Peace Dialogue Tables via Nine Executive Resolutions
detail: August 30, 2026 — Three days after ordering the extradition of five former Total Peace negotiators, President Abelardo De la Espriella's government issued nine executive resolutions formally shutting every remaining dialogue platform opened under predecessor Gustavo Petro's policy, El Tiempo reported. The closures cover the FARC dissident bloc led by alias 'Calarcá' (Resolution 342 of 2026, which cites an 'absence of will for peace' as grounds for ending the table), the Comandos de la Frontera border militia, and the Autodefensas Conquistadores de la Sierra Nevada paramilitary group. The move follows military strikes on rebel positions and completes the formal wind-down of Total Peace that De la Espriella signaled with the Aug. 27 extraditions. Gerson Arias of the Ideas for Peace Foundation warned the shift to a military-first approach 'will likely increase violence in the short term' as armed groups step up activity in the absence of a negotiation track.

title: US Strikes Iran's Larak Island, Iran Retaliates on Jordan and UAE Bases — Ending Month-Long Pause in Diplomatic Track
detail: August 30, 2026 — US Central Command struck two IRGC rocket launchers on Iran's Larak Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday after observing preparations to fire rockets carrying sea mines, marking the first US-Iran exchange of fire in a month and further burying hopes of reviving the Islamabad MOU framework that lapsed Aug. 17. Iran's IRGC retaliated Aug. 31 with missiles and drones against the US-operated King Hussein and Al Azraq bases in Jordan and a drone attack on the UAE's Al Minhad Air Base, saying it targeted areas where US forces and helicopters were stationed. Jordan's army said it intercepted eight missiles without confirming their origin; the UAE said it intercepted an Iranian drone over its waters and denied further Iranian claims. The flare-up comes as Pakistan's army chief Munir had reported 'highly positive' Tehran talks (Aug. 24-25) on reviving the MOU — talks this exchange now further complicates.
